newsitem.title: CHINA: CRICKET-SIXES MAY BE A HIT WITH CHINESE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SIXES MAY BE A HIT WITH CHINESE.

text.p: International cricket chiefs seeking to make their sport a truly global game may be encouraged by a six-a-side tournament in Shanghai.
The Shanghai Cricket Club staged the event at the weekend, with eight teams playing on a suburban soccer pitch.
Club captain Richard Graham said he hoped the tournament would help to spark interest in the sport among Chinese people.
"It's the first sixes competition in Shanghai ever, and the first time we have gathered together teams from Hong Kong and other cities of mainland China together to play cricket," said Graham.
"The Beijing team is skippered by a 100 percent Chinese named Bruce Wong who spent a few years in Australia where he picked up his English name and the rules of cricket.
"Cricket will become an Olympic sport before too long and when it is, the Chinese will be interested in it," added Graham.
